provenance: Official ClickHouse repository README and Apache license metadata
discoveries: ClickHouse is a column-oriented analytical database aimed at real-time reporting and large analytical workloads.
It is used by Jetstreamer as a durable high-throughput replay sink, with idempotent keys and retry/drain patterns documented there.
An OLAP database is useful for historical analysis but should not become the authoritative live position ledger without transactional invariants.
patterns: append event facts with stable identities
separate analytical projections from operational state
measure ingest lag and durable flush acknowledgments
sources.overlap: Could support future historical feature datasets; no ClickHouse runtime integration is currently required for source review.
risks: incorrectly using analytics storage for capital reservations
validation: benchmark representative replay data
test duplicate/restart and schema migrations
keep position/authorization state in appropriate durable transactional store

discoveries: Arrow is a columnar memory format and multi-language toolbox for interchange and in-memory analytics.
A language-neutral columnar schema can reduce data interchange overhead in offline feature pipelines.
It is not a source of chain truth or an execution component.
patterns: define typed columnar contracts
preserve null/missing distinction
version schemas across languages
sources.overlap: Possible offline dataset interchange; current live runtime is TypeScript and does not need Arrow for canonical ingestion.
validation: round-trip large integers and timestamps exactly
test missing vs zero semantics
pin Arrow format/library versions

discoveries: DataFusion is an extensible SQL query engine built on Arrow for analytical processing.
It could query columnar historical datasets without loading all data into memory.
Using it would add Rust infrastructure and does not address live canonicalization or fills.
patterns: push down filters to data sources
keep query schemas explicit
validate analytical results on small golden datasets
sources.overlap: Potential future offline analysis engine; overlaps DuckDB/ClickHouse and existing scripts conceptually.
validation: benchmark against reproducible dataset
compare query outputs with simple reference implementation
keep out of trading decision path until independently validated

provenance: Official Feast feature store README and docs
discoveries: Feast provides feature definitions, online/offline stores and point-in-time feature retrieval patterns.
Point-in-time retrieval can help prevent training leakage by ensuring features are computed from data available at the prediction time.
Feature store infrastructure does not guarantee source timestamps, lookahead-free labels, or Solana event correctness.
patterns: bind feature value to event/available timestamp
reconstruct point-in-time training views
separate online serving from offline backfill
sources.overlap: SYLPH has feature capture and training research; Feast would be a separate serving/data platform and not needed to correct source provenance.
validation: test temporal joins with delayed events
compare offline and online feature values
include failed/non-winner outcomes and execution costs

provenance: Official NautilusTrader repository README and architecture description
discoveries: NautilusTrader describes a deterministic event-driven trading engine with Rust-native performance and backtesting/live components.
It is a broad trading-engine framework, so importing it would duplicate SYLPH's existing feed, strategy, risk and execution authority layers.
Its deterministic simulation patterns may be useful for research comparisons but do not automatically model Solana execution/MEV.
patterns: replay immutable event streams deterministically
share strategy logic between backtest and runtime carefully
model venue-specific fills and fees explicitly
sources.overlap: High conceptual overlap with Fusion; no second trading engine should be added.
validation: compare event-replay determinism only
build Solana-specific cost and partial-fill model
do not route live orders through another authority

provenance: Official vectorbt README and project description
discoveries: vectorbt provides fast vectorized backtesting and portfolio analysis workflows.
Vectorized backtests can explore many hypotheses quickly but can conceal path-dependent execution, fill and fee constraints.
No live trading capability or SYLPH compatibility was validated.
patterns: screen parameter hypotheses with reproducible notebooks
model fees and slippage as explicit arrays
follow vectorized screening with event-level replay
sources.overlap: Potential offline research tool; does not replace execution-aware simulation.
validation: use walk-forward and token cohort splits
include nonfills, adverse selection, fees and priority costs
compare results to event-driven replay

provenance: Official Microsoft Qlib README and research framework description
discoveries: Qlib is an AI-oriented quant research platform supporting supervised, market-dynamics and reinforcement-learning workflows.
Framework breadth does not solve market-specific label leakage, token survivorship or execution realism.
Its equity-oriented conventions may need substantial adaptation for short-lived Solana launches.
patterns: version datasets and experiment configs
walk forward and compare baselines
track data and model provenance
sources.overlap: Potential research workflow reference, not an Engine runtime integration.
risks: complex ML infra before data quality
validation: define token-specific point-in-time dataset
compare simple baselines first
evaluate calibrated net return after costs on temporal holdout

provenance: Official LightGBM README and project description
discoveries: LightGBM is a gradient-boosted decision-tree framework for ranking, classification and regression.
Model choice cannot compensate for contaminated labels, point-in-time leakage, or biased winner-only samples.
It is a training/evaluation library, not a runtime signal source.
patterns: establish simple baseline and temporal splits
calibrate probabilities and ranking output
track model/data hashes
sources.overlap: Could be an offline research candidate; no dependency required in live TypeScript core.
validation: use nested walk-forward validation
include losers/failed launches and net execution outcomes
monitor calibration and drift

provenance: Official XGBoost README and supported interfaces
discoveries: XGBoost provides scalable gradient-boosted trees across multiple languages and distributed platforms.
It supports ranking/classification/regression tasks but does not provide domain-valid Solana outcome labels.
Model reproducibility requires pinned library, feature definitions, data split and random seeds.
patterns: serialize model and training metadata
compare ranking to calibrated baselines
keep training pipeline separate from execution process
sources.overlap: Potential research model library only; no live integration warranted.
validation: walk-forward holdout and repeated seeds
use realistic costs and failed orders
verify model output has no authority to bypass risk checks

provenance: Official CatBoost README and project description
discoveries: CatBoost implements gradient-boosted trees with support for categorical features and CPU/GPU training.
Categorical handling may fit token/program/source identifiers, but high-cardinality identity features can create memorization/leakage.
Library performance claims do not demonstrate prediction utility or net profitability.
patterns: audit categorical feature leakage
store model/version and data lineage
compare probability calibration and decision utility
sources.overlap: One possible offline modeling library; avoid multiple model stacks until dataset quality is established.
validation: hold out future time windows and token families
report net performance after realistic costs
test model degradation and calibration

provenance: Official Subsquid Pipes SDK README and feature description
discoveries: SDK supports TypeScript pipelines for streaming multi-chain data and writes to Postgres, ClickHouse, BigQuery or Parquet.
It advertises reorg handling and Solana decoding, making cursor/reorg semantics relevant for historical data pipelines.
Provider pipelines remain separate from SYLPH's canonical ingress and require independent coverage and provenance checks.
patterns: persist cursors and handle rollback
make sink idempotent
retain chain/source provenance with decoded rows
sources.overlap: Potential offline data acquisition alternative; duplicates some historical replay and decode infrastructure.
validation: pin SDK and source endpoint
test reorg rollback and duplicate sink writes
compare slot frontiers with independent finalized RPC

provenance: Official fast-check README and TypeScript property-testing documentation
discoveries: fast-check provides property-based testing for JavaScript/TypeScript with generated inputs and shrinking.
Shrinking failing cases can produce compact regression fixtures for bigint math, parsers and state transitions.
Property tests complement but do not replace protocol-specific golden fixtures.
patterns: assert invariants over generated numeric ranges
retain shrunk failure as deterministic regression
seed and report randomized runs
sources.overlap: Useful test-only tool for arithmetic and parser invariants; not a runtime dependency.
risks: weak properties may pass incorrect implementations
random seed reproducibility must be recorded
validation: define domain-specific invariants
bound test runs and capture seed
combine with known chain fixtures and mutation tests

discoveries: Hypothesis is a property-based testing library for Python with strategies for generated test inputs.
It is relevant to offline data/extraction scripts and ML feature validation if those paths are Python-based.
It does not integrate directly into Node test suites without a separate Python harness.
patterns: generate adversarial missingness and boundary cases
preserve minimized failing examples
test invariants across data schemas
sources.overlap: Could apply to Python dataset builders; current runtime tests use Node.
risks: generator properties may not match chain constraints
validation: scope to Python extraction pipeline
share fixtures with Node tests
pin Hypothesis version and deterministic profiles

provenance: Official MAPIE README and project description
discoveries: MAPIE implements conformal prediction intervals and risk-control methods compatible with scikit-learn.
Prediction intervals can communicate uncertainty but do not guarantee calibration under changing token distributions or dependent samples.
Uncertainty estimates must be evaluated on temporally held-out, point-in-time data.
patterns: report intervals rather than point estimate only
evaluate coverage and width over time
recalibrate under detected drift
sources.overlap: Potential offline uncertainty evaluation; no runtime trading authority role.
risks: exchangeability assumptions fail under regime shifts
misinterpreted intervals as guaranteed downside bounds
validation: test empirical coverage on future periods
include liquidity/fill uncertainty
label outputs advisory until risk controls independently validate

provenance: Official River README and online ML project description
discoveries: River provides incremental/online machine-learning tools for Python data streams.
Online updates introduce model state/versioning and feedback-loop risks, especially when labels arrive after token outcomes.
Delayed, selected trading outcomes can bias model updates and require strict label provenance.
patterns: version model state at each update
handle delayed labels explicitly
monitor drift and retain rollback checkpoints
sources.overlap: Potential research experimentation; no online learning is authorized in the SYLPH execution path.
risks: drift alerts confused with safe execution
validation: simulate delayed/missing labels
maintain offline replay and rollback
require independent review before any live model update
